Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $\delta\in R$. The object labels are the nonnegative integers $n=0,1,2,\ldots$. For labels $m,n$, place bottom points $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ and top points $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ along the rectangle from left to right on their respective edges. Their cyclic order is $t_1,\ldots,t_n,b_m,\ldots,b_1$. When $m=n=0$, the empty matching is included.

An $(m,n)$ **diagram** is a perfect matching of these $m+n$ boundary labels which is noncrossing: there are no four labels $a,b,c,d$ in cyclic order whose matched pairs are $\{a,c\}$ and $\{b,d\}$. A picture consists of disjoint arcs realizing the matching; equality is equality of the matching, so planar deformation that fixes the boundary does not change a diagram. If $m+n$ is odd, there are no such diagrams. Write $\mathcal D(m,n)$ for this set and define the $R$-module

$$M_R(m,n):=R^{(\mathcal D(m,n))},$$

the free $R$-module on the set of diagrams ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]). In particular, its diagram basis is empty when $m+n$ is odd.

For basis diagrams $D:m\to n$ and $E:n\to p$, stack $E$ above $D$ and identify the $n$ matching boundary points. The resulting finite graph has degree two at each identified point, where degree means the number of incident arcs. Each component is a path joining two exterior boundary points or a closed cycle. Remove every cycle and multiply the remaining exterior matching by $\delta^c$, where $c$ is the number of removed cycles. Denote this output by $E\circ D$ and extend the rule $R$-bilinearly to a map $M_R(n,p)\times M_R(m,n)\to M_R(m,p)$. A following result proves closure of these operations on the diagram modules and the category axioms.

The matching $1_n:n\to n$ pairs each bottom point to the top point directly above it. Horizontal juxtaposition, with the left diagram placed first, defines $m\otimes m'=m+m'$ on object labels and $D\otimes D'$ on basis diagrams; extend it $R$-bilinearly to the modules. A following result proves that these operations give a strict monoidal category.

For $1\le i<n$, let $d_i\in M_R(n,n)$ be the diagram with a cap joining top points $i,i+1$, a cup joining bottom points $i,i+1$, and vertical through strands at every other position. Define $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ to be the $R$-module $M_R(n,n)$ with bilinear multiplication $xy:=x\circ y$ and distinguished element $1_n$. A following result proves that it is a unital associative $R$-algebra and identifies it with the endomorphism algebra at object $n$.

The left factor is stacked above the right factor. The loop value is $\delta$; no invertibility or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is part of these data.

For every commutative ring $R$, loop value $\delta\in R$, and objects $m,n,p,q\ge0$, the raw diagram data of [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]] form a strict monoidal category $\mathcal{TL}_R(\delta)$ with hom-modules $M_R(m,n)$ and the stated $R$-bilinear stacking composition. Composition is associative, the identity diagrams are two-sided identities, and horizontal juxtaposition is a strict monoidal bifunctor with unit object $0$. Consequently $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal{TL}_R(\delta)}(n)=\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ is a unital associative $R$-algebra whose underlying $R$-module is free on its noncrossing pairing diagrams.

For every $n\ge0$, each basis diagram in $\mathcal D(n,n)$ is a finite product of the elementary diagrams $d_1,\ldots,d_{n-1}$ from [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]. The product can be chosen so that no intermediate stack creates a closed cycle. Therefore the set of diagrams lies in the unital subalgebra of $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ generated by these diagrams.

Put $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$. For a commutative $A$-algebra $R$, let $V_n$ be the free $R$-module on binary words of length $n$, with $V_0=R$. The cup and cap maps are

$$c(1)=q(01)+(10),\qquad b(01)=1,\quad b(10)=q^{-1},\quad b(00)=b(11)=0.$$

Insertion of these maps in adjacent positions defines a representation

$$\rho_n:\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_R(V_n).$$

Over $A$ this map has an $A$-linear left inverse, and the same left inverse works after every base change to $R$. In particular, it is injective over every such $R$. It preserves the number of ones, and on the local ordered basis $00,01,10,11$ the generator $d_i$ has zero $00,11$ blocks and middle block

$$\begin{pmatrix}q&1\\1&q^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.$$

Horizontal reflection of an endomorphism diagram is represented by matrix transpose.

For $0\le k\le n$, let $G_{n,k}(Q)$ be the polynomial $\sum_w Q^{\operatorname{inv}(w)}$, summed over binary words with $k$ ones and $n-k$ zeros, where $\operatorname{inv}(w)$ counts pairs with a one to the left of a zero. There is a unique polynomial $B_{n,k}(T)\in\mathbb Z[T]$ such that

$$B_{n,k}(q+q^{-1})=q^{-k(n-k)}G_{n,k}(q^2).$$

It agrees as a rational-function identity with $[n]!/([k]![n-k]!)$; its value at a specialized loop parameter is the polynomial value, without division by vanishing factorials.

For a field $K$, $\delta\in K$, recurrence quantum characteristic $\ell$, and $p=\operatorname{char}K$, every $B_{n,k}(\delta)$ for $0\le k\le n$ is nonzero exactly as follows: if $\ell=\infty$, at every finite $n$; if $\ell<\infty$ and $p>0$, when $n<\ell$ or $n=a\ell p^{i-1}-1$ with $i\ge1$ and $1\le a<p$; if $\ell<\infty$ and $p=0$, when $n<\ell$ or $n=a\ell-1$ for a positive integer $a$.

Let $K$ be a field, $\delta\in K$, and $n\ge0$. A normalized idempotent $e\in\mathrm{TL}_n(K,\delta)$ with $d_ie=0$ for $1\le i<n$ exists if and only if every $B_{n,k}(\delta)$ of [[lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion]], $0\le k\le n$, is nonzero. Every such $e$ also satisfies $ed_i=0$ and is unique. This is a field assertion; it makes no integral-ring descent claim.

derivations.claim: By propagation in [F1], the span of the nonidentity diagrams is an ideal, so $\varepsilon$ is a ring homomorphism; that ideal is spanned by nonempty generator words. Thus the linear equations $d_ie=0$, $\varepsilon(e)=1$ imply $ae=\varepsilon(a)e$ for every $a$, and in particular $e^2=e$. Horizontal reflection defines an anti-involution $*$ fixing generators and preserving $\varepsilon$. The element $f=ee^*$ is killed by the generators on both sides and has augmentation $1$. Right annihilation gives $fe=f$, while left annihilation of $e$ gives $fe=e$; hence $e=f$ is two-sided. For two such elements $e,e'$, the same argument gives $ee'=e$ by right annihilation of $e$ and $ee'=e'$ by left annihilation of $e'$. They are equal. These arguments use no division and work over every commutative coefficient ring.

First work over any commutative ring $C$ containing a unit $q$ with $\delta=q+q^{-1}$. In the weight-$k$ word module of [F2], the equations for the common kernel are $a_{u10v}=-q a_{u01v}$. Successive adjacent swaps reduce each word to $0^{n-k}1^k$ and change its inversion number by one. Thus this kernel is exactly the free line generated by $v_k=\sum_w(-q)^{\operatorname{inv}(w)}w$, whose baseword coefficient is $1$. If $e$ is normalized, step 1.1 and symmetry in [F2] put both the columns and rows of its weight block in this line. First comparing the baseword column, and then each row, expresses the block as $\alpha_kv_kv_k^{\mathsf T}$ for some $\alpha_k\in C$. Every nonempty generator word kills $v_k$ by its rightmost factor; consequently $(e-1)v_k=0$. Comparing the baseword coefficient in $ev_k=v_k$ gives $\alpha_kG_{n,k}(q^2)=1$. In particular all these Gaussian values are units. This conclusion remains valid with nilpotents or zero divisors.

For general $R$, put $R'=R[q]/(q^2-\delta q+1)$. Division by this monic quadratic gives a unique representative $a+bq$: subtract successive leading terms to prove existence, while a nonzero multiple of a monic polynomial has degree at least two, proving uniqueness. Thus $R'=R\oplus Rq$ as an $R$-module, $R$ injects into $R'$, and $q$ is a unit with inverse $\delta-q$. Base-changing an existing $e$ to $R'$ and applying step 2.1 makes $G_{n,k}(q^2)$ a unit. By [F3] the factor $q^{k(n-k)}$ is a unit, so $B=B_{n,k}(\delta)$ is a unit in $R'$. Write its inverse $a+bq$. The equality $B(a+bq)=1$ in the indicated free basis gives $Ba=1$ in $R$. Hence $B$ is already a unit in $R$.

To prove sufficiency construct a universal projector with only the named denominators. Use an indeterminate $q$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, and its fraction field $L=\mathbb Q(q)$. Facts [F3, F4] give a normalized projector $p\in\mathrm{TL}_n(L,q+q^{-1})$. Step 2.1 determines each of its weight blocks as $v_kv_k^{\mathsf T}/G_{n,k}(q^2)$. Let $S=A[G_{n,k}(q^2)^{-1}:0\le k\le n]\subset L$. That matrix has entries in $S$. Apply the base-changed linear left inverse of [F2] to obtain a diagram-coefficient vector $z\in\mathrm{TL}_n(S,q+q^{-1})$. After extension to $L$ it equals $p$. Since $S$ injects into $L$ and the diagram module is free, the same identities already hold over $S$: $\varepsilon(z)=1$, $d_iz=zd_i=0$ and $z^2=z$. Thus no unproved assertion about the image or centralizer of a quantum-group action is needed.

Suppose now every $B_{n,k}(\delta)$ is a unit in $R$, and form $R'$ as in step 3.1. Fact [F3] makes all evaluated $G_{n,k}(q^2)$ units in $R'$. Therefore evaluation defines a ring homomorphism $S\to R'$: send a fraction $a/\prod G_{n,k}^{e_k}$ to the evaluated numerator times the inverses of the indicated evaluated denominators; the cross-multiplied equality defining equal fractions remains true after evaluation. Specialize $z$ from step 3.2 to get a normalized annihilator $e'\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R',\delta)$. Let $\pi:R'\to R$ be the $R$-linear coefficient projection $\pi(a+bq)=a$ and apply $\pi$ to every diagram coefficient of $e'$, obtaining $e\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. Left multiplication by each $d_i$ has matrix entries in $R$, so it commutes with this coefficient projection. Hence $d_ie=0$ and $\varepsilon(e)=\pi(1)=1$. Step 1.1 now makes $e$ the required unique two-sided idempotent. The projection is used only on these linear equations; it need not preserve multiplication.

Any homomorphism $R\to T$ sends the diagram coefficients and their defining linear identities to those over $T$, so the image of the projector is the unique projector there by step 1.1. For $n=0,1$ there are no generator equations, the identity is the projector, and every binomial in the row is $1$. The same argument includes the zero ring under the convention that its identity is its unique element. This establishes all stated implications and boundaries.

derivations.claim: It suffices to perform computations for left modules: send a right module to the left module with $a\cdot v=v\cdot a^*$, where $*$ is diagram reflection. This is an exact equivalence preserving Hom direction, induction and restriction. Fix a square root of $q$ and put $g_i=q^{1/2}1-q^{-1/2}d_i$. Expanding with [F1] gives $g_i^{-1}=q^{-1/2}1-q^{1/2}d_i$ and $g_ig_{i+1}g_i=g_{i+1}g_ig_{i+1}$. Let $T_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n$ close the last top endpoint to the last bottom endpoint externally on the right, removing any resulting loop with factor $\delta$. This is an $A_n$-bimodule map by the matching rule. Define $M_n=g_n\cdots g_2g_1^2g_2\cdots g_n$ and $F_n=T_n(M_n)$; set $F_0=\delta$. Every summand of $M_n$ has an even total number of square-root factors, so $F_n$ has coefficients in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, independent of the chosen square root.

For clarity give a basis proof of the induction sequence. In left-module notation put $h_r=d_rd_{r+1}\cdots d_n$ for $1\le r\le n$, and $h_{n+1}=1$. A state $d$ is $r$-admissible when it has no adjacent arc at an index $i\ge r$. The tensors $h_r\otimes d$ with $d$ $r$-admissible, including all $1\otimes d$, span $A_{n+1}\otimes_{A_n}V_{n,p}$. First, a diagram word is a sum of $h_ru$ with $u\in A_n$: reverse a spanning Jones normal form from [F1]. Its initial ascending block is either $h_r$ or contains no $d_n$, and every later block lies in $A_n$. The surjection from the presented algebra to the diagram algebra is supplied by the local relations, so this spanning assertion applies to diagram words. Next, if $d$ has its largest adjacent arc at $s\ge r$, write $d=d_sf$. For $n\ge3$ this can be done without division: move the endpoint immediately outside that adjacent arc through the arc, so applying $d_s$ restores $d$ and creates no loop. If $s=1$ use site $3$; otherwise use site $s-1$. The outside site is either a defect or an endpoint of another arc, and reconnecting its former partner supplies the inverse state $f$. Now the relations give $h_r\otimes d=h_{s+2}\otimes d_r\cdots d_{s-1}d$. The latter state is $(s+2)$-admissible: the adjacent arc at $s$ has moved to $r$, all intervening endpoints shift by two, and the tail beyond $s+1$ still has no adjacent arc. Repetition, increasing $r$, proves spanning. At $n=1,2$ the same conclusion is checked on the at most two states, except $n=2,p=1,\delta=0$, when the needed factorization $d=d_1f$ fails.

The braid relations give $g_iM_n=M_ng_i$ for $i<n$. To see this directly, commute $g_i$ past all $g_j$ with $|j-i|>1$ in the descending and ascending strings; the remaining equality is $g_ig_{i+1}g_i=g_{i+1}g_ig_{i+1}$ on each side of the middle string. This proves the equality inductively in the length of the strings, starting with $g_1g_2g_1^2g_2=g_2g_1^2g_2g_1$. Bimodule linearity of $T_n$ gives $g_iF_n=F_ng_i$, hence $d_iF_n=F_nd_i$. Thus $F_n$ is central. Reversing the palindromic word $M_n$ and reflecting its closure leaves it unchanged, so $F_n^*=F_n$.

Compute $F_n$ on the state $z_p$ with adjacent arcs $(1,2),(3,4),\ldots,(2p-1,2p)$ and all remaining sites defects. At a cup, expansion of the two adjacent crossings uses the identities $d_ig_{i+1}g_i=-d_id_{i+1}$ and $g_ig_{i+1}d_i=-d_{i+1}d_i$; for example the first is $qd_i-d_id_{i+1}-\delta d_i+q^{-1}d_id_{i+1}d_i=-d_id_{i+1}$. The two minus signs on the two sides of each cup cancel. Thus each initial cup can be removed without changing the coefficient of $z_p$. For the $t=n-2p$ defect strands, expand the auxiliary strand successively from its first crossing. A smoothing connecting two defects vanishes in the standard quotient. There are two remaining continuations: following the auxiliary strand on its two sides gives respectively $q^t\delta-q^{t-1}=q^{t+1}$ and $q^{-t}\delta-q^{-t+1}=q^{-(t+1)}$. The factors arise by choosing the identity smoothing at each subsequent crossing until the final cap; that cap either closes a loop or chooses the second smoothing, giving the displayed two terms on each side. Hence the coefficient of $z_p$ is $f_{n,p}$. For generic $q$, [F3] makes the form nondegenerate. Capping $z$ against $y$ and then attaching $x$ gives the rank-one diagram operator $z\mapsto\phi(y,z)x$, because lower-propagating terms vanish. Thus every nonzero vector generates the standard, which is simple. Centrality now makes $F_n$ scalar on the entire standard: over $\mathbb C$ a central operator has an eigenvalue, whose nonzero eigenspace is the simple module. Since the action matrices and $f_{n,p}$ are Laurent polynomial in $q$, this scalar identity extends to every $q\ne0$.

On the submodule and quotient in [F2], $F_{n-1}$ acts by $f_{n-1,p}$ and $f_{n-1,p-1}$. Their difference is $-(q-q^{-1})(q^{n-2p+1}-q^{-(n-2p+1)})$. Under the noncritical and $q\ne\pm1$ hypotheses it is nonzero. The operator on the restriction satisfies $(F_{n-1}-f_{n-1,p})(F_{n-1}-f_{n-1,p-1})=0$, because each factor kills its respective subquotient. Its two spectral projections therefore give an invariant direct sum splitting the restriction sequence.

Append an adjacent arc at sites $n+1,n+2$ to $d$, obtaining $\bar d\in V_{n+2,p+1}$. The map $\Phi(u\otimes d)=u\bar d$ into $V_{n+2,p+1}\downarrow$ is balanced and $A_{n+1}$-linear: elements of $A_n$ act only on the first $n$ sites. Its image of $h_r\otimes d$ has its rightmost adjacent arc at $r$; deleting that arc recovers $d$. Conversely every $(n+2,p+1)$-state has a rightmost adjacent arc; delete it at position $r$, and the remaining state is $r$-admissible. These two operations are inverse, so the spanning tensors in step 1.2 map bijectively to the link-state basis. They are therefore a basis and $\Phi$ is an isomorphism, except in the stated exceptional case. Applying the restriction sequence [F2] to $V_{n+2,p+1}$ now gives the asserted induction sequence. Applying step 4.1 at rank $n+2$ splits it whenever $(n,p)$ is noncritical, since $n+2-2(p+1)+1=n-2p+1$.

Consequently it factors through the quotient $V_{n+1,p}$ into the submodule $V_{n+1,p+1}$, giving a nonzero map between these adjacent reflected standards. Explicitly, lift a quotient vector to the induction, apply $F_{n+1}-f$, and use the inverse of the submodule injection; the result is independent of the lift because this operator kills the submodule.

Work over $\mathbb C$, with $q\ne0$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$. Write $A_n=\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ and $V_{n,p}=W_{n,n-2p}(\mathbb C,\delta)$. There is a central, reflection-invariant element $F_n\in A_n$ acting on $V_{n,p}$ by
$$f_{n,p}=q^{n-2p+1}+q^{-(n-2p+1)}.$$
When $q\ne\pm1$ and $(n,p)$ is noncritical, restriction splits as $V_{n,p}\downarrow=V_{n-1,p}\oplus V_{n-1,p-1}$. Except at $(n,p,\delta)=(2,1,0)$, induction has a natural exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow V_{n+1,p+1}\longrightarrow V_{n,p}\uparrow\longrightarrow V_{n+1,p}\longrightarrow0,$$
which splits when $(n,p)$ is noncritical. Here induction of a right module means $V\otimes_{A_n}A_{n+1}$.

If $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)\ge2$ and $p<p'$ are a pair reflected in a single intervening critical line, meaning $0<p'-p<\kappa$ and $p=p'+r(n,p')-\kappa$, then
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(V_{n,p},V_{n,p'})\ne0.$$
Out-of-range standard modules are zero. Statements about a splitting omit zero summands.

Let $q\in\mathbb C^\times$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, $n\ge0$, and $0\le p\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. Put $t=n-2p$, and let $G_{n,p}$ be the Gram matrix of the link-state form on $W_{n,t}(\mathbb C,\delta)$ in its link-state basis. Set

$$d_{n,r}=\binom nr-\binom n{r-1},\qquad \binom n{-1}=0.$$

Then

$$\det G_{n,p}=\prod_{j=1}^{p}\left(\frac{[n-2p+1+j]_q}{[j]_q}\right)^{d_{n,p-j}}.$$

The empty product for $p=0$ is $1$. The right side is interpreted as its polynomial continuation in $\delta$ at parameter values where an individual displayed quotient has a removable zero-over-zero form.

Let $q\in\mathbb C^\times$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, $n\ge0$, and $0\le p\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. Put $t=n-2p$, let $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)$, and let $\phi_{n,t}$ be the link-state capping form on $W_{n,t}(\mathbb C,\delta)$. If $(n,p)$ is critical in the sense of [[def-temperley-lieb-complex-critical-labels-and-reflection]], then $\phi_{n,t}$ is nondegenerate and $W_{n,t}(\mathbb C,\delta)$ is simple.

Let $R$, $\delta$, $n$, $t$ and $W_{n,t}(R,\delta)$ be as in [[def-temperley-lieb-link-state-standard-modules]]. For link states $x,y$, let $x^*$ denote reflection across a horizontal line. The diagram $y\circ x^*:t\to t$ is either $\delta^c1_t$ for some $c\ge0$ or has fewer than $t$ propagating components. Define $\phi_{n,t}(x,y)=\delta^c$ in the first case and $0$ in the second, and extend $R$-bilinearly. Then $\phi_{n,t}$ is symmetric and satisfies

$$\phi_{n,t}(x\cdot a,y)=\phi_{n,t}(x,y\cdot a^*)$$

for all $x,y\in W_{n,t}(R,\delta)$ and $a\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. Here $a^*$ is reflection across a horizontal line. The matrix of $\phi_{n,t}$ in the link-state basis is the Gram matrix obtained by reflecting and capping two link states, with one factor $\delta$ for each closed loop.

Let $n\ge0$ and let $t$ satisfy $0\le t\le n$ and $n-t$ even. Put $a=(n-t)/2$, the number of arcs in a link state, and use the convention $\binom{n}{a-1}=0$ when $a=0$. Then the link-state basis $T_{n,t}$ of $W_{n,t}(R,\delta)$ has cardinality

$$|T_{n,t}|=\binom{n}{a}-\binom{n}{a-1}.$$

In particular, $W_{n,t}$ is free of this rank over $R$, independently of $\delta$.

Let $q\in\mathbb C^\times$. Define $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)$ if $q^2$ has finite multiplicative order, and $\kappa=\infty$ otherwise. For integers $n\ge0$ and $p$ with $0\le p\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, set the defect label $t=n-2p$; here $p$ counts arcs and $t$ counts defects. The pair $(n,p)$ is **critical** at $q$ when $\kappa<\infty$ and $\kappa\mid(t+1)$, equivalently $q^{2(t+1)}=1$. If $\kappa=\infty$, no pair is critical. When $\kappa=1$ every allowed pair is critical.

For finite $\kappa\ge2$ and a noncritical pair, write uniquely
$$t+1=k\kappa+r,\qquad k\ge0,\quad 1\le r<\kappa.$$
Its reflection label across the next critical line is
$$p^\sharp=p+r-\kappa.$$
This reflected label is called present only when $p^\sharp\ge0$; it then automatically satisfies $p^\sharp\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. If $p^\sharp<0$, there is no label in range on that side. A critical label is treated as a singleton under reflection. These are arithmetic label conventions; they do not by themselves assert radical, composition-factor, Hom-space, or projective-cover formulas.

The order $\kappa$ is kept separate from the recurrence quantum characteristic $\ell$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-quantum-integers-and-quantum-characteristic]]. For $q=\pm1$, $\kappa=1$ while the complex recurrence quantum characteristic is $\infty$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit and $\delta\in R$. Define the quantum integers by

$$[0]_\delta=0,\qquad [1]_\delta=1,\qquad [r+1]_\delta=\delta[r]_\delta-[r-1]_\delta\quad(r\ge1).$$

The **quantum characteristic** of $(R,\delta)$ is the least positive integer $\ell$ with $[\ell]_\delta=0$, if one exists, and $\ell=\infty$ otherwise. No element of $R$ is inverted in this definition.

For $q\in\mathbb C^\times$ and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, write $[r]_q=[r]_\delta$. If $q\ne\pm1$, this agrees with $(q^r-q^{-r})/(q-q^{-1})$; at $q=\pm1$ the recurrence gives $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}$. For complex-parameter classification, write $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)$, with $\kappa=\infty$ when $q^2$ has infinite order. If $q\ne\pm1$, the quantum characteristic equals $\kappa$ when $\kappa<\infty$ and is $\infty$ otherwise. At $q=\pm1$, $\kappa=1$ but the complex quantum characteristic is $\infty$, because $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}\ne0$ for every positive $r$.

For a field $K$ of positive characteristic $p$, set $p(0)=1$ and, when $\ell<\infty$, set $p(i)=\ell p^{i-1}$ for $i\ge1$. In characteristic zero and finite $\ell$, the finite digit scale is $p(1)=\ell$; the separate characteristic-zero criterion below uses $a\ell-1$ for arbitrary positive integers $a$. If $\ell=\infty$, every finite index is already in the range $n<\ell$.

derivations.claim: First work at generic $q$. The rightmost-defect submodule has nondegenerate form by [F2], so its orthogonal complement is invariant and maps isomorphically to the restriction quotient. The smaller standards are simple by their rank-one diagram operators; an invariant form on such a standard is a scalar multiple of its nondegenerate standard form, because their associated maps into the dual differ by an endomorphism, and an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional complex simple module is scalar (take any eigenvalue). Subtracting the submodule projection from quotient basis lifts gives a unitriangular Gram splitting $G_{n,p}=U^{\mathsf T}(G_{n-1,p}\oplus\alpha_{n,p}G_{n-1,p-1})U$. Compute its scalar as follows. Group the link states into the four types: $n,n-1$ both defects; $n$ a defect and $n-1$ on an earlier arc; $(n-1,n)$ an arc; and $n$ on an arc ending earlier than $n-1$. Put $A=G_{n-2,p}$, $B=G_{n-2,p-1}$ and write the smaller-rank matrix as $G_{n-1,p}=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A&AV_0\\V_0^{\mathsf T}A&V_0^{\mathsf T}AV_0+\alpha_{n-1,p}B\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. In the current off-diagonal Gram block the first column block is $(0,B)^{\mathsf T}$: types one and three have unmatched defects, while cutting the terminal arc in types two and three removes no closed component. The type-three diagonal block is $\delta B$, since the shared terminal arc closes one loop. If $(X,Y)^{\mathsf T}$ is the first column block of the projection coefficient matrix, multiplication by $G_{n-1,p}$ gives $AX+AV_0Y=0$ and $V_0^{\mathsf T}AX+(V_0^{\mathsf T}AV_0+\alpha_{n-1,p}B)Y=B$. Thus $X=-V_0Y$ and $Y=\alpha_{n-1,p}^{-1}I$. Its quadratic contribution is $\alpha_{n-1,p}^{-1}B$ after the four $V_0^{\mathsf T}AV_0$ terms cancel with coefficients $1-1-1+1$. Comparing the type-three block gives $\alpha_{n,p}=\delta-\alpha_{n-1,p}^{-1}$. At $n=2p$, deleting the terminal site closes exactly one additional component, so $G_{2p,p}=\delta G_{2p-1,p-1}$ and $\alpha_{2p,p}=\delta$. The recurrence solves to $\alpha_{n,p}=[n-2p+2]_q/[n-2p+1]_q$ by the quantum-integer recurrence. If the $A$ block is empty it is omitted; the same cancellation still holds. Now at a noncritical root, the two eigenvalues used for [F1] differ by $-(q-q^{-1})(q^{n-2p+1}-q^{-(n-2p+1)})\ne0$. The spectral projector onto the rightmost-defect summand is $(F_{n-1}-f_{n-1,p-1})/(f_{n-1,p}-f_{n-1,p-1})$. Its entries are rational functions regular at the root; subtracting this projection from each standard quotient lift gives a unitriangular splitting matrix $U$, also regular there. Since $F_{n-1}^*=F_{n-1}$ and the eigenvalues differ, the two summands are orthogonal. For generic $q$ this is exactly the orthogonal splitting just computed, since the submodule form is nondegenerate and its orthogonal complement is unique. Thus this Gram matrix identity is an identity of rational matrices regular at every noncritical root, and specializes there. This continuity argument applies to the entire matrix identity, rather than inferring a rank from a specialized determinant. If $n=2p$, there is only the quotient summand and direct capping gives $G_{2p,p}=\delta G_{2p-1,p-1}$, the same formula with $\alpha=[2]/[1]=\delta$.

Since $\kappa\ge2$, $q\ne\pm1$; hence $[a]_q=0$ precisely when $\kappa\mid a$. At a noncritical label the denominator of $\alpha$ is nonzero and its numerator vanishes precisely when $r=\kappa-1$. The kernel dimension of the specialized block form in step 1.1 is therefore $\dim R_{n-1,p}+\dim V_{n-1,p-1}$ in that case, and $\dim R_{n-1,p}+\dim R_{n-1,p-1}$ otherwise. Critical labels give zero by [F3]; the all-defect form is $(1)$, giving $R_{n,0}=0$. For $n\ge1$, subtraction from [F4] gives the companion recursion, with initial $\dim L_{0,0}=1$: $\dim L_{n,p}=\dim V_{n,p}$ at critical labels; at noncritical labels it is $\dim L_{n-1,p}$ if $r=\kappa-1$, and $\dim L_{n-1,p}+\dim L_{n-1,p-1}$ otherwise.

Prove the reflected-dimension formula by induction on $n$, with out-of-range labels assigned dimension zero. Write $a=p+r-\kappa$. If $r\notin\{1,\kappa-1\}$, neither predecessor is critical. Their reflection indices are respectively $a-1$ and $a$, so induction and step 2.1 give $\dim R_{n,p}=\dim L_{n-1,a-1}+\dim L_{n-1,a}$. The reflected label $a$ has remainder $\kappa-r$, which is also neither $1$ nor $\kappa-1$; its companion recursion gives exactly $\dim L_{n,a}$.

When $\kappa=2$, every noncritical label has $r=1=\kappa-1$ and both predecessors are critical. The radical recursion gives $\dim R_{n,p}=\dim V_{n-1,p-1}=\dim L_{n-1,p-1}$. Since $a=p-1$ and the companion recursion at $(n,a)$ also has remainder $1$, this is $\dim L_{n,a}$. The same formula holds for $n=2p$: it gives $\dim R_{2p,p}=\dim V_{2p-1,p-1}=\dim V_{2p,p}$, as required by the identically zero form.

If $r=\kappa-1$ and $\kappa>2$, the predecessor $(n-1,p-1)$ is critical, while $(n-1,p)$ has reflected index $a-1$. Consequently $\dim R_{n,p}=\dim L_{n-1,a-1}+\dim V_{n-1,p-1}$. Here $a=p-1$, and criticality gives $V_{n-1,p-1}=L_{n-1,a}$. The companion recursion at $(n,a)$ has remainder $1\ne\kappa-1$, so this sum is $\dim L_{n,a}$. If $r=1$ and $\kappa>2$, $(n-1,p)$ is critical and its radical is zero; the reflection of $(n-1,p-1)$ has index $a$. Thus $\dim R_{n,p}=\dim L_{n-1,a}$. The reflected label at rank $n$ has remainder $\kappa-1$, whose companion recursion is precisely $\dim L_{n,a}=\dim L_{n-1,a}$.

The initial $p=0$ case has $a<0$ and zero radical. All predecessor terms whose indices leave the allowed range are zero. In particular the recursions in the preceding cases give zero when $a<0$; when $a=0$ they use the initial all-defect dimension $1$. These boundary rules also cover $n=0,1$. The induction establishes the stated formula for present reflected labels and the zero radical for absent labels.
